source.title: Forgetful Attention: A Trainable Support-Vector Memory with Certified Selection and Exact Unlearning

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study examines deletion and later reactivation in an explicit support-vector context memory, not unlearning or recovery attacks on LLM weights or model knowledge.
record.gate_note: The results concern a separate explicit-memory mechanism. They do not test the claim versions about LLM unlearning, fine-tuning recovery, activation edits, quantization, or prompt-based recovery. The relevant reserve-key and later-admission findings are recorded as related results with versions ["none"].
record.test_reason: The study concerns deletion of keys from an explicit support-vector context memory (an SVDD gate over stored keys), not unlearning of knowledge from LLM weights. It neither tests nor relies on LLM unlearning or recovery attacks. Machine unlearning work (Cao & Yang, Bourtoule et al., ECO) appears only in related work. 'cites_only' fits better than 'discusses', since the paper does not discuss the shallow-unlearning claim itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The authors conclude that an exactly zero coefficient certifies current-state removal and that active-key deletion has a fixed-cap refit target. A current-state certificate does not justify permanent pruning across later admissions. A checked wrapper completes the sequential numerical audit with rescues. The paper makes no claim about LLM unlearning.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an explicit support-vector memory with coefficient-based removal, rather than gradient ascent, Who's Harry Potter, RMU, or other LLM unlearning methods.
record.method_sensitivity: A later admission can change whether a previously zero-weight key is active.

fits_no_version.finding: In a three-key support-vector memory, evicting a zero-coefficient key leaves the readout unchanged (4.6e-9). A later faraway admission makes that key active (coefficient 0.033), and the pruned state then differs from the full-history reference (gate score 4.1e-3).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A current-state deletion certificate in an explicit context memory does not guarantee equivalence to the full-history memory after future admissions.

record.problems: The key reactivation example is a three-key construction, not an LLM experiment. The paper also states that its result does not establish a sufficient general admission rule.
record.rows_left_out: Other numerical deletion audits, selection experiments, and training results were left out because they do not measure LLM unlearning or recovery; see Sections 4.3–4.6 and Appendices A–B.

untested.parts: All: no LLM unlearning method, forget/retain accuracy or attack.
All: no activation-direction ablation or access-vs-deletion analysis of LLM weights.
All: no counter-method against LLM unlearning attacks.

record.verdict_notes: Relation changed from 'discusses' to 'cites_only'; the T6 tranche is kept. The paper explicitly disclaims transfer to model keys, editing pretrained weights and erasure of prior copies, so none of its results bear on versions A–F. The deletion audits, selection experiments and training results in Sections 4.3–4.6 and Appendices A–B are correctly left out.

versions.untested_parts: LLM unlearning performance, retention of general ability, and simple recovery attacks.
Recovery by fine-tuning on unrelated, loosely related, or forgotten examples.
Activation-direction ablation and whether LLM unlearning blocks access rather than deleting knowledge.
Recovery by quantizing unlearned LLM weights.
Recovery through rephrasing, jailbreaks, other languages, or in-context information.
A counter-method to the listed LLM-unlearning recovery attacks.

rows.subject: three-key construction
rows.operation_detail: Remove a key with exactly zero support-vector coefficient without re-solving.
rows.measure: Readout difference; the gate-score change is also reported.
rows.value: readout difference 4.6 × 10−9; gate-score change less than 10−12
rows.note: The text says the third key's coefficient was exactly zero and the readout change was consistent with the current-state certificate up to numerical residual.
rows.check: Concerns zero-coefficient key eviction in an explicit memory; no LLM knowledge, unlearning method or recovery attack. The values are correct (readout 4.6e-9, gate-score change <1e-12), but the state relative to any version is not determinable.

rows.subject: three-key construction
rows.size_stated: three initial keys; one later admission
rows.operation_detail: Admit a faraway token and solve over the full history after the reserve key has been discarded.
rows.measure: Reactivation of the discarded key and gate-score difference from the full-history reference.
rows.value: formerly reserve key coefficient 0.033; gate-score difference 4.1 × 10−3
rows.note: This is a result about future admissions in the explicit support-vector memory, not recovery of LLM knowledge.
rows.check: Reactivation of a discarded reserve key (coefficient 0.033; gate-score gap 4.1e-3) after a later admission in a three-key construction. Superficially analogous to recovery, but it is a property of an explicit memory's solve, not recovery of unlearned LLM knowledge. Values are correct.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
